{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, or Sham) affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the five-level factor",
    "For Success (binary), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA",
    "Given substantial sample size imbalance across paradigms (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505 and Bright Visual Only n=3323), use Type III sums of squares to account for unequal group sizes",
    "Consider Welch's ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis as robust alternatives if variance homogeneity violated"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous variables showing significant ANOVA results: pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD for equal variances, or Games-Howell for unequal variances",
    "For Success (binary): pairwise comparisons of proportions with confidence intervals",
    "Focus comparisons on Combined vs each unimodal condition (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and vs Sham to assess multimodal enhancement",
    "Compare Sham vs active stimulation conditions to establish baseline effects",
    "Examine ICMS Only vs Visual conditions to assess modality-specific contributions"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Control family-wise error rate using the Holm-Bonferroni method across all pairwise tests within each response variable, then apply a Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the five response variables to balance Type I error control with power given the large sample size (N=76655)",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression (softmax regression) is the appropriate predictive model because Stim Paradigm is a categorical response with five unordered levels. This directly models P(Stim Paradigm = k | performance variables) without requiring arbitrary numeric encoding. Alternative: Random Forest or Gradient Boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM) for non-linear relationships and interactions, particularly given the likely complex, non-linear relationships between performance metrics and stimulation type. Given the class imbalance (Combined ~64% of data vs ~4% for Bright Visual Only), use class-weighted loss or stratified sampling. Evaluate using multinomial log-loss, macro-averaged F1, and confusion matrix analysis. If ordinality assumptions can be justified (Sham < unimodal < Combined), an ordered logit model could be tested, but this requires theoretical justification.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice (random effects structure may be needed given 8 mice with repeated measures)",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk on residuals; given N>75000, central limit theorem provides robustness but check extreme skewness in Time-to-Target (max=201.4 suggests right tail)",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test; expected violation given unequal group sizes and likely paradigm-specific variance (e.g., Sham may show higher variability)",
    "Multicollinearity: Correlation matrix among the five performance variables; AD and Path Efficiency may correlate",
    "Complete separation check for multinomial logistic regression (quasi-complete separation possible given large group differences)",
    "Class balance: Address severe imbalance (Combined: 48846, Bright Visual Only: 3323) via weighting or resampling"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows superior performance: lowest Time-to-Target, highest Success rate, highest Path Efficiency, highest Average Speed, and lowest AD (more direct paths)",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: highest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, lowest Path Efficiency, lowest Speed, highest AD (most erratic paths)",
    "ICMS Only and Visual-only conditions expected intermediate, with potential differences between Dim vs Bright visual stimulation",
    "Large effect sizes expected given substantial mean differences likely exist (Combined n=48846 dominates sample)",
    "Multinomial logistic regression expected to classify Combined trials well but struggle with Bright Visual Only vs Dim Visual Only discrimination due to smaller sample sizes and potential similarity"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe group imbalance (Combined 63.7% vs Bright Visual Only 4.3%) reduces power for fair comparisons and biases ANOVA toward Combined mean",
    "No mouse-level random effects in current plan despite 8 mice with repeated measures (78687 total trials, ~9800 per mouse) - violates independence assumption",
    "AD interpretation as angular dispersion assumes circular statistics validity; values near 0 and 1 may be boundary-constrained",
    "Success is binary but treated separately; no unified multivariate analysis of all five metrics",
    "Temperature=0.75 and prompt template specifics may affect reproducibility; no cross-validation of analysis pipeline specified",
    "Temporal dynamics ignored: learning effects, fatigue, and session effects not modeled",
    "Causal inference limited: observational comparison of paradigms, not randomized within-mouse crossover design explicitly confirmed"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect for each performance variable, followed by multinomial logistic regression with cross-validated class weights to predict Stim Paradigm; include temporal covariates (trial number, session) to account for learning/fatigue; conduct sensitivity analysis excluding extreme Time-to-Target outliers (>20s, ~1.5% of data); and perform permutation-based post-hoc tests to handle unequal variances without distributional assumptions."
}
